subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Child Labor in Coffee
description: One-minute skill: Child Labor in Coffee.

hook.text: The US Department of Labor lists coffee as a product commonly produced using child labor in multiple countries.

buildup.text: When prices crash, families who can't afford hired workers send children to pick cherries instead of going to school.

discovery.text: An estimated 1.5 million children work in coffee farming—many in hazardous conditions with chemicals and sharp tools.

twist.text: The root cause isn't cultural acceptance—it's poverty. When families earn enough, children go to school instead.

climax.text: The most effective lever against child labor in coffee is simply paying farmers a living wage.

punchline.text: Low prices don't just hurt farmers. They steal childhoods.

quiz.question: What is the root cause of child labor in coffee farming?
options: Poverty—when families can't afford workers, children pick instead
